advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Thread `force_reclaim=True` through `run_git_write` (or plumb a parameter) so the txn transition/claim, compact, delete, and init write-lock-held git ops also force-reclaim a young orphan index.lock, matching the event_append helpers.
evidence: src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:257: `    result = _with_index_lock_retry(` — call site inside run_git_write passes no force_reclaim (defaults to False)
src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:126: `    cp = run_git_write(tracker_dir, *args, check=False)` in `_git`, whose docstring says 'self-heals git's .git/index.lock contention'
src/rebar/_commands/txn.py:177: `    handle = _acquire_write_lock(tracker_dir)` and txn.py:301 — the transition/claim path holds the exclusive write lock across its git ops
src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py:247: docstring of run_git_write refers to 'the transition/claim path' as a caller

ABSENCE: the diff adds force_reclaim=True only to the four event_append helpers; no corresponding change to run_git_write or its callers, so a young orphan index.lock in the txn/compact/delete/init locked write still waits the full _INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S (300s)
advisory.finding: The write-lock-held git seam `run_git_write` (used by the txn transition/claim, compact, delete, and init write paths) still calls `_with_index_lock_retry` without `force_reclaim=True`, so it defaults to `force=False` and remains exposed to the same 300s Mode B orphan-index.lock cascade this change eliminates for event_append. The commit's invariant (store git runs under the exclusive write lock → any index.lock is an orphan) applies equally to `txn._git`, which holds the write lock via `_acquire_write_lock`, but that path was not updated.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a `force_reclaim: bool = True` parameter to `run_git_write` (all its callers hold the write lock) and pass it into `_with_index_lock_retry(..., force_reclaim=force_reclaim)`, or set `force_reclaim=True` at the call site on gitutil.py:257.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a force=True TOCTOU test: plant a young/stale lock, inject a peer replacing it (different inode) via the `_reclaim_probe` seam, call `_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock(tracker, force=True)`, and assert the replacement lock survives.
evidence: gitutil.py:141 `if (st2.st_dev, st2.st_ino) != (st.st_dev, st.st_ino): return  # replaced by a different file (a fresh lock) → do NOT remove`
gitutil.py:143 `if not force and time.time() - st2.st_mtime <= _INDEX_LOCK_STALE_S:` — the age abort is bypassed under force, so only the inode check remains
gitutil.py:117-118 docstring claim: `The device+inode identity re-validation below is STILL applied under force, so a TOCTOU replacement is never removed.`

The existing TOCTOU test calls the helper with default force=False: test_stale_lock_reclaim_write.py:95 `gitutil._reclaim_if_stale_index_lock(tracker)` and its comment relies on the fresh-mtime abort (test_stale_lock_reclaim_write.py:86-91) which force disables

ABSENCE: `search_files force=True` in tests/ shows the only force-path test (test_event_append_index_lock.py:122) reclaims a STATIONARY young lock; no mid-flight `_reclaim_probe` swap is injected under force
advisory.finding: The force=True TOCTOU re-validation (device+inode identity guard) is untested. The diff disables the age re-check under force (gitutil.py:143 `if not force and ...`), leaving the device+inode check at gitutil.py:141 as the SOLE guard preventing a peer's mid-flight replacement lock from being clobbered — the invariant the new docstring explicitly asserts ("device+inode identity re-validation below is STILL applied under force"). No test drives the `_reclaim_probe` seam with `force=True`, so a regression that skips/negates the inode guard on the force path (which would delete a live peer's fresh index.lock and risk index corruption) would go undetected.
scenarios: A future refactor gates the device+inode check behind `not force` (mirroring the age gate) — a peer's fresh live lock is clobbered under the write lock and the index is corrupted, with the whole test suite still green.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test alongside `test_stale_index_lock_not_reclaimed_when_inode_replaced_midflight` that monkeypatches `gitutil._reclaim_probe` to unlink+recreate the lock (new inode) and calls `_reclaim_if_stale_index_lock(tracker, force=True)`, asserting `lock_file.exists()` and the fresh content is preserved — proving the device+inode guard still fires when the age gate is bypassed.
